extracted.intended_audience: shippers, carriers, package designers, and regulatory compliance officers involved in transport of Class 7 (radioactive) materials
extracted.subtask_description: U.S. DOT regulatory requirements for classification, packaging, labeling, documentation, testing, and transport of Class 7 (radioactive) materials, including limits, package types (excepted/industrial/Type A/Type B/fissile), and procedures for LSA and SCO materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: LSA-I definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Low Specific Activity material group LSA-I as defined in the regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LSA-I is one of the LSA groupings used to classify materials for packaging and transport requirements. See associated provisions for permitted packaging/transport (e.g., §173.427 and Table 6). Specific examples and numeric limits for LSA groups appear elsewhere in the subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: LSA-II definition
rubrics_metrics.description: LSA-II: water with tritium concentration up to 0.8 TBq/L (20.0 Ci/L) or other radioactive material with activity distributed throughout and average specific activity not exceeding 10^-4 A2/g for solids and gases and 10^-5 A2/g for liquids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LSA-II categorization determines allowable packagings and conveyance activity limits; see §173.427 for packaging and transport conditions and Table 6 for industrial package types.

rubrics_metrics.name: LSA-III definition
rubrics_metrics.description: LSA-III: Solids (e.g., consolidated wastes, activated materials), excluding powders, that meet the requirements of §173.468 and in which (i) radioactive material is distributed throughout a solid or collection of solids or uniformly in a solid binding agent; (ii) material is relatively insoluble or intrinsically contained in relatively insoluble material such that leaching loss per package in water for seven days would not exceed 0.1 A2; and (iii) estimated average specific activity (excluding shielding) does not exceed 2 × 10^-3 A2/g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LSA-III classification invokes specific packaging integrity and transport controls; reference §173.468 and §173.427 for packaging and conveyance rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low toxicity alpha emitters definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural uranium; depleted uranium; natural thorium; uranium-235 or uranium-238; thorium-232; thorium-228 and thorium-230 when contained in ores or physical and chemical concentrates; and alpha emitters with a half-life of less than 10 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in contamination and surface activity limit tables and SCO definitions (different numeric limits apply for beta/gamma and low toxicity alpha emitters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum normal operating pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum gauge pressure that would develop in a containment system during a period of one year, in the absence of venting or cooling, under the heat conditions specified in 10 CFR 71.71(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant to Type B(M) designation and multilateral approval determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multilateral approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of a package design or shipment by the relevant Competent Authority of the country of origin and of each country through or into which the package or shipment is to be transported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not include approval from a country merely overflown without scheduled stop. Multilateral approval impacts which Type B packages may be used for international shipments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural thorium definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Thorium with the naturally occurring distribution of thorium isotopes (essentially 100 percent by weight of thorium-232).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine applicability of certain exceptions and classification as unirradiated/natural material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normal form Class 7 (radioactive) material
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 7 material which has not been demonstrated to qualify as 'special form Class 7 (radioactive) material.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiates handling, packaging and A1/A2 calculations between normal and special form materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excepted package definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A packaging together with its excepted Class 7 (radioactive) materials as specified in §§173.421-173.426 and 173.428.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excepted packages are excepted from many specification packaging, labeling and shipping paper requirements if they meet the limits and conditions in those sections, but are still subject to specific markings and reporting provisions (§173.422).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial package definition and types
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial package is a packaging that, together with its LSA material or SCO contents, meets the requirements of §§173.410 and 173.411. Industrial packages are categorized as Industrial package Type 1 (IP-1), Type 2 (IP-2), or Type 3 (IP-3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 6 in §173.427 lists which IP type is required by content (LSA-I, II, III; SCO-I, II; solids/liquids/gases) and whether exclusive use is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type A package definition and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A packaging that, together with its radioactive contents limited to A1 or A2 as appropriate, meets the requirements of §§173.410 and 173.412 and is designed to retain containment and shielding under normal transport conditions as demonstrated by tests in §173.465 or §173.466; Type A does not require Competent Authority approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type A packages must meet specific tests and activity limits tied to A1/A2 values (see §173.433 and §173.435). Documentation and test evidence may be required for certain authorized Type A packages (§173.415).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type B package definition (including B(U) and B(M))
rubrics_metrics.description: A packaging designed to transport quantities greater than an A1 or A2 quantity that, together with contents, is designed to retain containment and shielding under normal and hypothetical accident test conditions set forth in 10 CFR part 71. Type B(U) requires unilateral approval (country of origin); Type B(M) requires multilateral approval of design and possibly conditions of shipment (those with maximum normal operating pressure >700 kPa or relief device releasing material under 10 CFR part 71 accident conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type B packages are subject to NRC/Competent Authority approval and detailed international standards (10 CFR part 71 and IAEA regs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fissile material package definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A packaging, together with its fissile material contents, which meets requirements for fissile material packages described in subpart E of 10 CFR 71. A fissile material package may be Type AF, Type B(U)F, or Type B(M)F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fissile packaging has specific criticality safety and approval requirements; see §173.417 for authorized packagings and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging (assembly) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: For Class 7 materials, packaging means the assembly of components necessary to ensure compliance with packaging requirements, which may include receptacles, absorbents, spacing structures, insulation, shielding, service equipment, venting and pressure relief devices, and shock-absorbing devices; conveyance/tie-down/auxiliary equipment may sometimes be designated as part of the packaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines what components are evaluated for compliance and testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A systematic program of controls and inspections applied by each person involved in the transport of radioactive material which provides confidence that a standard of safety prescribed in this subchapter is achieved in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates implementation of QA programs across transport lifecycle to ensure compliance with packing, testing, inspection and operational requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radiation level definition and neutron flux conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Radiation level means the radiation dose-equivalent rate expressed in mSv/h (mrem/h). Neutron flux densities may be converted into radiation levels according to Table 1 (list of energies and equivalent flux densities for 0.01 mSv/h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Table 1 to convert neutron fluence rates at various energies to an equivalent radiation level for labeling and compliance measurements; interpolate linearly between energies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radioactive contents definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A Class 7 (radioactive) material together with any contaminated or activated solids, liquids and gases within the packaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contents definition is used to calculate package activity, A1/A2 limits, and to determine applicable packaging requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radioactive instrument or article definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Any manufactured instrument or article (e.g., clock, electronic tube, apparatus) having Class 7 material in gaseous or non-dispersible solid form as a component part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such instruments/articles may be excepted from many requirements if they and their packaging meet the specific conditions in §173.424 (activity limits, radiation levels, enclosure by non-active components, contamination limits, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Radioactive material threshold definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Any material containing radionuclides where both the activity concentration and the total activity in the consignment exceed values specified in §173.436 or values derived per §173.433.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the tables and calculation methods in §§173.433–173.436 to determine if material qualifies as Class 7 and which packaging/labeling/transport rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special form Class 7 material requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Either an indispersible solid radioactive material or a sealed capsule containing radioactive material that (1) is a single solid piece or sealed capsule that can be opened only by destroying the capsule; (2) has at least one dimension ≥5 mm; and (3) satisfies the test requirements of §173.469.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special form encapsulations designed per earlier provisions before certain dates may continue in use subject to legacy allowances; otherwise meet current paragraph (3) test requirements for qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific activity definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific activity of a radionuclide means the activity of the radionuclide per unit mass of that nuclide. For material with the nuclide uniformly distributed, it is the activity per unit mass of the material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in computing activity concentration and comparing to exemption limits and LSA classification thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface Contaminated Object (SCO) definitions (SCO-I and SCO-II)
rubrics_metrics.description: SCO means a solid object not itself radioactive but with radioactive material on its surface. SCO-I and SCO-II are phases defined by specific non-fixed and fixed contamination limits averaged over 300 cm^2 for beta/gamma/low-toxicity alpha and for other alpha emitters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric limits: SCO-I non-fixed accessible ≤4 Bq/cm^2 for beta/gamma and low-tox alpha (0.4 Bq/cm^2 for other alpha); fixed accessible ≤4×10^4 Bq/cm^2 (4×10^3 for other alpha); SCO-II has higher thresholds (non-fixed accessible ≤400 Bq/cm^2 or 40 Bq/cm^2 for other alpha; fixed accessible ≤8×10^5 Bq/cm^2 or 8×10^4 for other alpha). These determine packaging and transport requirements (§173.427 and Table 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport index (TI) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The dimensionless number (rounded up to the next tenth) on the package label to designate degree of carrier control during transport; TI = (maximum radiation level in mSv/h at 1 m) × 100 (equivalent to mrem/h at 1 m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for load planning, segregation, and radial separation requirements on conveyances and for placarding and labeling controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type A quantity definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A quantity of Class 7 material whose aggregate radioactivity does not exceed A1 for special form or A2 for normal form as given in §173.435 or determined per §173.433.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines whether material may be shipped in Type A packaging or requires Type B/fissile packaging and approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type B quantity definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A quantity of material greater than a Type A quantity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires Type B packaging and regulatory approval/tests per 10 CFR part 71 and related sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unilateral approval definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of a package design solely by the Competent Authority of the country of origin of the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant to Type B(U) packages authorized for international shipments where only unilateral approval is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unirradiated thorium definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Thorium containing not more than 10^-7 grams uranium-233 per gram of thorium-232.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine exceptions and classification as unirradiated material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unirradiated uranium definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Uranium containing not more than 2×10^3 Bq of plutonium per gram of uranium-235, not more than 9×10^6 Bq of fission products per gram of uranium-235, and not more than 5×10^-3 g of uranium-236 per gram of uranium-235.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thresholds used to classify uranium as unirradiated for exception and packaging rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uranium—natural, depleted, enriched definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural uranium: chemically separated uranium with natural isotopic distribution (~99.28% U-238, 0.72% U-235). Depleted uranium: less mass% U-235 than natural. Enriched uranium: greater mass% U-235 than 0.72%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions used where regulatory limits or exceptions differ by uranium enrichment or form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial packagings must conform to ISO 1496-1
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial package designs (per §173.411) must be designed to conform to the standards prescribed in ISO 1496-1:1990(E) 'Series 1 Freight Containers—Specification and testing—Part 1: General cargo containers,' excluding dimensions and ratings (IBR §171.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design conformity to ISO 1496-1 (excluding dimensions/ratings) is required for industrial packagings, as adopted by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized Type A packages: DOT Spec 7A and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized Type A packages include DOT Specification 7A Type A general packaging. Each offeror of a Specification 7A package must maintain on file for at least one year after the latest shipment complete documentation of tests and an engineering evaluation or comparative data showing compliance, and provide to DOT on request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign-made Type A packagings that meet IAEA TS-R-1 and bear 'Type A' marking may be used domestically and for export if the offeror obtains and maintains applicable test and engineering documentation per paragraph (a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized Type B packages: approval and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Type B(U) or Type B(M) packagings that meet 10 CFR part 71 and have been approved by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission may be shipped pursuant to §173.471. Type B(U)/B(M) packagings meeting IAEA TS-R-1 with revalidated foreign Competent Authority Certificate are authorized only for export/import.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continued use of older DOT specification Type B packagings is authorized only until specified transition dates if conforming to prior subchapter requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized fissile materials packages and UF6 heel allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: Fissile materials containing not more than A1 or A2 must be packaged in specified packagings (e.g., any packaging listed in §173.415 limited to materials specified in 10 CFR Part 71 Subpart C; any Type AF/Type B(U)F/Type B(M)F meeting 10 CFR 71 standards; or those meeting IAEA Section VI with revalidated foreign certificates for export/import). Residual 'heel' of enriched solid UF6 may be transported without protective overpack in metal cylinders meeting requirements of §173.415 and §178.350 and §173.420, with allowable contents shown in Table 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables provide allowable UF6 'heel' weights by cylinder diameter and enrichment; additional handling and packaging criteria reference USEC-651 or ANSI N14.1 and specific overpack specifications (e.g., 20PF/21PF).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uranium hexafluoride packaging, design, testing and limits (§173.420)
rubrics_metrics.description: Packagings for >0.1 kg of UF6 must be cleaned per ANSI N14.1, designed/fabricated/inspected/tested/marked per ANSI N14.1, DOT-106A specs or, for certain older ASME Code units, conform to the edition in effect at fabrication and maintain minimum shell/head thicknesses. Each package must withstand hydraulic test at ≥1.4 MPa (200 psi) without leakage; withstand tests in §173.465(c) and 10 CFR 71.73(c)(4); UF6 must be solid; volume of solid UF6 limits at 20°C (61% or 62% of certified capacity); internal pressure <101.3 kPa; periodic inspection/repairs per N14.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive prescriptive construction, testing and maintenance requirements apply; non-fissile UF6 <0.1 kg may be shipped under §§173.24/173.24a/173.410.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excepted packages for limited quantities (§173.421)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Class 7 material with activity per package not exceeding limited quantity package limits specified in Table 4 (§173.425) and its packaging are excepted from many subchapter requirements for specification packaging, labeling (except UN number marking), and, if not hazardous substance/waste, shipping papers, and requirements of this subpart, provided conditions in §173.421 are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excepted status depends on meeting Table 4 activity limits and the specific conditions in §173.421; even excepted packages remain subject to some marking/reporting/training requirements (§173.422).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional requirements for excepted packages (§173.422)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excepted packages prepared under §§173.421/173.424/173.426/173.428 are not subject to additional subchapter requirements except: (a) outside marked with 4-digit UN identification number preceded by 'UN'; (b) incident reporting per §§171.15/171.16; (c) reporting of decontamination per mode-specific sections; (d) training requirements of subpart H of part 172; and (e) shipping paper requirements for hazardous substances/waste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when excepted from many requirements, these specific obligations (marking/reporting/training/shipping papers for hazardous materials) still apply and must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excepted packages for radioactive instruments and articles (§173.424)
rubrics_metrics.description: A radioactive instrument or article and its packaging are excepted from many requirements if: (a) packaging meets general design requirements of §173.410; (b) activity of instrument/article ≤ limits in Table 4; (c) total activity per package ≤ limits in Table 4; (d) radiation level at 10 cm from unpackaged instrument ≤0.1 mSv/h; (e) active material completely enclosed by non-active components; (f) radiation level at package surface ≤0.005 mSv/h (or 0.02 mSv/h for exclusive use domestic shipments); (g) nonfixed external surface contamination ≤ limits in §173.443(a); (h) package does not contain >15 g U-235 (except per §173.426); and (i) package prepared for shipment per §173.422.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meets narrow conditions for excepted status; check each clause (a)–(i) to ensure eligibility for exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excepted packages for articles containing natural uranium or thorium (§173.426)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufactured articles whose sole Class 7 content is natural uranium, unirradiated depleted uranium or natural thorium, and packaging, are excepted from specification packaging, labeling (except UN number), and, if not hazardous, shipping papers and other subpart requirements if conditions in §173.426 are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar in effect to §173.424 but specific to articles with those particular materials; eligibility depends on satisfying conditions enumerated in the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport requirements for LSA material and SCO (general) (§173.427(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to other applicable subchapter requirements, LSA materials and SCO (unless excepted) must be packaged per (b) and transported in accordance with: (1) external dose rate ≤10 mSv/h at 3 m; (2) quantity in any conveyance may not exceed limits in Table 5; (3) LSA/SCO containing fissile material must conform to §173.453; (4) packaged/unpackaged materials must conform to contamination control limits (§173.443); (5) external radiation levels may not exceed §173.441; and (6) special conditions for exclusive use consignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets principal operational limits that control whether materials require special packaging, conveyance limits, or must follow fissile/accident-condition rules; consult referenced sections and tables for numeric values and packaging types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive use shipment conditions for LSA/SCO (§173.427(a)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: For LSA/SCO consigned as exclusive use: (i) consignor loads and consignee unloads the originally loaded conveyance/freight container; (ii) no loose radioactive material in conveyance (no leakage where conveyance is packaging); (iii) materials must be braced to prevent shifting under normal transport; (iv) offeror must provide specific exclusive use maintenance instructions to carrier and include with shipping paper; (v) except unconcentrated ores, transport vehicle must be placarded per subpart F of part 172; (vi) for domestic transport only, packaged/unpackaged Class 7 materials containing <A2 are excepted from marking/labeling but exterior must be stenciled/marked 'RADIOACTIVE—LSA' or 'RADIOACTIVE—SCO' as appropriate and 'RQ' for hazardous substances; (vii) air transport prohibited except when in industrial package per Table 6 or in authorized Type A or Type B package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusive use status relaxes some requirements but imposes operational controls (loading/unloading, bracing, instructions, placarding, marking) and restrictions on air transport; ensure shipping papers include required instructions and markings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging options for LSA material and SCO (§173.427(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: LSA material and SCO must be packaged as follows unless excepted: (1) in an industrial package (IP-1/IP-2/IP-3) subject to Table 6 limits; (2) in a DOT Specification 7A Type A package; (3) in any Type B/B(U)/B(M) packaging authorized under §173.416; (4) for domestic exclusive use of less than an A2 quantity only, in packaging meeting §§173.24/173.24a/173.410; or (5) for exclusive use transport of liquid LSA-I, in specified tank cars (Specification 103CW, 111A60W7) or cargo tank motor vehicles (MC 310/311/312/331 or DOT 412) with bottom openings prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of packaging depends on LSA group, whether contents are solids/liquids/gases, exclusive use status, and whether quantities exceed A1/A2; consult Table 6 for IP assignments and Table 5 for conveyance activity limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpackaged transport conditions for LSA-I and SCO-I (§173.427(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: LSA-I and SCO-I may be transported unpackaged under conditions: (1) unpackaged material (other than ores with only naturally occurring radionuclides) must be transported so there will be no escape of contents or loss of shielding under normal transport; (2) each conveyance must be under exclusive use (except when only transporting SCO-I with accessible/inaccessible contamination ≤4.0 Bq/cm^2 for beta/gamma and low-tox alpha and 0.4 Bq/cm^2 for other alpha); (3) for SCO-I suspected of non-fixed contamination exceeding specified inaccessible-surface values, measures must ensure material not released into conveyance or environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tight operational controls and exclusive use generally required for unpackaged LSA-I/SCO-I; check contamination values and take measures to prevent release if inaccessible non-fixed contamination is suspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: LSA/SCO exceeding packaging limits must follow 10 CFR part 71
rubrics_metrics.description: LSA and SCO that exceed the packaging limits in §173.427 must be packaged in accordance with 10 CFR part 71.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When activity or packaging limits surpass §173.427 allowances, full Type B (or other 10 CFR part 71) packaging, testing and approval regimes apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conveyance activity limits (Table 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 5 lists conveyance activity limits for LSA and SCO: 1) LSA-I: No limit; 2) LSA-II and LSA-III (non-combustible solids): No limit; 3) LSA-II and LSA-III (combustible solids and all liquids/gases): 100 A2; 4) SCO: 100 A2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Table 5 to determine maximum aggregate activity per conveyance for different material types; when limits are exceeded, different packaging/approval is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial package integrity requirements (Table 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 6 prescribes which industrial packaging type (IP-1/IP-2/IP-3) is required for various contents and whether exclusive use or non-exclusive use shipments apply (e.g., LSA-I solids: IP-1 both exclusive/non-exclusive; LSA-II liquids/gas: IP-2 exclusive/non-exclusive with IP-3 for non-exclusive liquids/gases, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select IP type per content (LSA group/SCO status) and mode (exclusive vs non-exclusive) as specified in Table 6; failure to use the correct IP type violates packaging prescriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empty Class 7 packaging exception conditions (§173.428)
rubrics_metrics.description: A packaging previously containing Class 7 materials and emptied as far as practical is excepted from shipping paper and marking (except UN ID number marking) requirements provided specified conditions are met, including that the outer surface of any uranium or thorium in its structure is covered with an inactive sheath made of metal or other substantial material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emptying must be to the extent practical and special covering of uranium/thorium structures is required; other subsection conditions (not fully reproduced here) also apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity limits for Type A and Type B packages (§173.431)
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on activity contained in a Type B(U) or Type B(M) package are those prescribed in §§173.416 and 173.417, or in the applicable approval certificate under §§173.471, 173.472 or 173.473.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine allowed activity for Type B packagings by reference to the cited sections or the specific approval certificate for the package design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining basic radionuclide values and listing on shipping papers/labels (§173.433)
rubrics_metrics.description: For radionuclides listed in tables §173.435 and §173.436, A1 and A2 values and activity concentration/consignment exemption values are provided. For radionuclides not listed, values in Tables 7 or 8 may be used or other basic radionuclide values approved by the Associate Administrator (or multilateral approval for international transport). When calculating A1/A2 for unlisted radionuclides, chemical form (solubility class) may be considered; single decay chains in natural proportions with daughters not exceeding certain half-life thresholds may be treated as a single nuclide; mixtures must satisfy sum-of-fractions formulae; alternative mixture calculations and exempt concentration/consignment formulae are provided; grouping rules apply when individual activities are unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided tables and the detailed formulae for mixtures and groupings (paragraphs (d)(1)–(7) and (e)-(f)). For unlisted nuclides or unusual chemical forms, obtain prior approval from the Associate Administrator or obtain multilateral approval for international shipments. Calculations include using A1/A2 fractional sums and f(i) fraction methods for mixtures and exemptions; when identity/activity partial information exists, grouping uses lowest applicable A1/A2 or exempt values for conservative compliance.
